s: Remove exact duplicates first (SELECT DISTINCT on the business columns).
Compare each row with the previous one for the same customer (LAG); keep it only if a tracked attribute changed, or if it's the first.
ValidTo = the next version's ValidFrom (LEAD), or 9999-12-31 for the current one; IsCurrent = 1 when there is no next version.
Assign the surrogate key with ROW_NUMBER over the natural key and date (in a real warehouse: an IDENTITY or sequence that never reuses numbers).

code.title: dim_customer as SCD type 2
src: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS dim_customer;
CREATE TABLE dim_customer (CustomerSK INT, CustomerID VARCHAR(20), Segment VARCHAR(40), HomeRegionKey INT,
LoyaltyTier VARCHAR(20), ValidFrom DATE, ValidTo DATE, IsCurrent INT);
-- CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT isn't SQL Server syntax; a CTE followed by INSERT works in both
WITH feed AS (
SELECT DISTINCT CustomerID, EffectiveDate, Segment, HomeRegionKey, LoyaltyTier FROM customer_changes
compared AS (
SELECT f.*,
LAG(Segment)       OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY EffectiveDate) AS PrevSegment,
LAG(HomeRegionKey) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY EffectiveDate) AS PrevRegion,
LAG(LoyaltyTier)   OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY EffectiveDate) AS PrevTier,
ROW_NUMBER()       OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY EffectiveDate) AS n
FROM feed AS f
versions AS (
SELECT CustomerID, EffectiveDate AS ValidFrom, Segment, HomeRegionKey, LoyaltyTier
FROM compared
WHERE n = 1 OR Segment <> PrevSegment OR HomeRegionKey <> PrevRegion OR LoyaltyTier <> PrevTier
INSERT INTO dim_customer (CustomerSK, CustomerID, Segment, HomeRegionKey, LoyaltyTier, ValidFrom, ValidTo, IsCurrent)
SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY CustomerID, ValidFrom) AS CustomerSK,
CustomerID, Segment, HomeRegionKey, LoyaltyTier, ValidFrom,
COALESCE(LEAD(ValidFrom) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY ValidFrom), '9999-12-31') AS ValidTo,
CASE WHEN LEAD(ValidFrom) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY ValidFrom) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS IsCurrent
FROM versions;
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_changes) AS FeedRows,
COUNT(*) AS Versions, SUM(IsCurrent) AS CurrentRows, COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS Customers
FROM dim_customer;

s: Join orders to dim_customer on CustomerID AND OrderDate >= ValidFrom AND OrderDate < ValidTo (half-open interval: exactly one version matches).
Store the resulting CustomerSK on the fact at load time, so reports don't need the range join.
Type 2: Segment, LoyaltyTier, HomeRegionKey (analysed over time). Type 1: name spelling, email, phone (corrections; history not useful).

code.title: Versions of the example customer
src: SELECT CustomerID, LoyaltyTier, ValidFrom, ValidTo, IsCurrent
FROM dim_customer
WHERE CustomerID = '{{dw_example_customer}}'
ORDER BY ValidFrom;

code.title: Point-in-time join (facts get the version valid on the order date)
src: SELECT o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, d.CustomerSK, d.LoyaltyTier
FROM orders AS o
JOIN dim_customer AS d
ON d.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
AND o.OrderDate >= d.ValidFrom AND o.OrderDate < d.ValidTo;

dw-keys-1.note: Only 120 customers are in the change feed; orders for other customers need an initial version (or the Unknown member) to join.

s: Add an Unknown member (CustomerSK = -1) to the dimension.
When a fact's natural key isn't in the dimension: create an inferred member (CustomerID known, attributes "Pending") and point the fact to it. Never drop the fact.
When the real row arrives, update the inferred member in place (type 1 update of a placeholder), then continue type 2 from there.
Keys that never arrive stay visible: report "facts on inferred members older than 7 days" as a data quality check.

code.title: Which early orders can be resolved?
src: -- one row per known customer, so the join never multiplies orders (SQL Server can't SUM over EXISTS)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS EarlyOrders,
SUM(CASE WHEN c.CustomerID IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Resolvable,
SUM(CASE WHEN c.CustomerID IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS StillUnknown
FROM early_orders AS e
LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT CustomerID FROM customer_changes) AS c ON c.CustomerID = e.CustomerID;
